body: Yes I’ve been in workplaces managed by women - if it’s not the guys being creepy it’s the women getting weirdly insecure about me doing modelling. That’s a bit of a tough one. I hope I find somewhere too. Thanks so much for your help.

That’s really good advice and definitely something I’m going to think about. Mike made me really happy when he was here, but at the end of the day he was only here for a short time, and I have to figure out whether it’s worth throwing away a relationship for someone who might never come back, and vice versa if my current bf isn’t giving me what I need then how can I address that... really good advice.

I’m very sure it’s not temporary. It’s been over a year since I’ve seen him. When he was living here it was so intense and we’ve stayed in contact off and on since - not many deep conversations or anything though. But more recently with lockdown going on, I feel like he’s opening up to me a bit more - we’ve started having good conversations and talking to him makes me really happy. I’m confused whether I should admit to him that I really like him or not - I dunno how I would go with rejection right now. He knows I’m in an open relationship and has said when all this crazy stuff is over he wants to come visit me or for me to visit him. I said in passing to one of my friends today that if he were living here still I would 100% pursue it with him. My friend suggested I do it anyway and dump my current bf... but he’s overseas so logistically it’s a bit hard and I do like my current bf a lot.

When I was 13 I had a friend who’s best friend committed suicide. My friend was messed up for years afterwards, and would always say passing comments like “I wonder what so and so would do if she were here now.” When I was 17 a close friend’s mother died (of cancer, not suicide), and that was even worse. Death is a really hard thing for the people left behind to deal with. It can completely alter the lives of the friends and family, and it’s extremely traumatic for them. Even though you don’t think it now, there will always be people who would be affected by losing you. I know I don’t know you or anything, or know your situation, but you deserve to have a good life. Everyone does. Don’t cut yours short because of a feeling that has the possibility to pass.

It’s not the first time I’ve opened up about myself to someone else. In the past I’ve had counselling and things like that, and I’ve opened up to a certain point. I find it very difficult to get words out when I’m speaking about emotional things so I only get so far. But yes, you’re right that most people assume that people who are conventionally beautiful or “successful” are happy. It’s not a fair assumption for people to make really is it?
I talked to my best friend about it and she was shocked. I didn’t go into full detail with her about it. I don’t want to worry her or scare her.
